models_evaluated: XGBoost semantic model (LLM text embeddings of serialized EHR variables)

links.outcome: Comparative AUROC of numerical vs embedding-based pipelines on same data across 6 ICU tasks
links.effect: Numerical model beat semantic model for 5 of 6 tasks (mortality AUROC 0.9010 vs 0.8351); semantic model better for 30-day readmission (0.6618 vs 0.5900); errors only partly overlapping.
links.quote: Representation choice shapes not only aggregate performance but also which patients are misclassified, supporting hybrid architectures over winner-take-all replacement.

links.outcome: Clinical subgroup failure phenotypes where each model's errors concentrate
links.effect: Semantic model mortality errors concentrated in coagulopathic, hypoalbuminemic, hepatic, and high-density records; numerical model readmission errors concentrated in creatinine-centered phenotypes in sparse, imputed, low-volatility records.
links.quote: Semantic model mortality errors concentrated in coagulopathic, hypoalbuminemic, hepatic, and high-density records; NM readmission errors were dominated by creatinine-centered phenotypes in sparse, imputed, low-volatility records.

unlisted_practices: Hybrid architectures combining numerical and embedding-based representations rather than replacing one with the other

screen.reason: Evaluates failure phenotypes, error overlap, and representations between numeric and LLM embedding-based clinical risk prediction pipelines on the MIMIC-III dataset without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
